h: Concorde, the zoo and Cribbs Causeway
p: Patchway is in aviation country. Just down the road at Filton, Aerospace Bristol tells the story of the region's aircraft industry, and its star attraction is the very last Concorde ever to fly, displayed in its own hangar. You can step on board and imagine supersonic travel, which goes down well with plane-mad kids and grown-ups alike. Pairing that with a bounce makes for a high-flying day out.

Cribbs Causeway shopping centre is also close by, with restaurants and shops for a post-jump refuel or a bit of retail therapy. Bristol Zoo Project, now based just off the M5 near Cribbs Causeway, is another big family attraction in the area, with large habitats, woodland walks and adventure play. Check the opening details before you go, but it pairs nicely with a session at AirHop for a full day north of the city.

Back in the city itself, the harbourside is the heart of Bristol's family scene. Brunel's SS Great Britain is a fantastic hands-on museum on board the famous steamship, while M Shed tells the story of the city and its people for free. We The Curious, the science centre on Millennium Square, is full of experiments and a planetarium. And of course, the Clifton Suspension Bridge spans the Avon Gorge, a great place for a stroll and a photo. A tip for AirHop: if you've got an under-5, check the times for the dedicated little ones' area so they get the best of it. Bring a bag for shoes and coats, as it gets busy at peak times.
